verdict.rationale: Unleash documents self-hosting an open-source distribution: you can set up Unleash Open Source in your own environment with Docker, by cloning the repository and starting it with Docker Compose. A community member independently recommends it as an open-source, self-hosted LaunchDarkly alternative. However, the evidence shows that features such as RBAC, change requests, SSO, SCIM and custom roles come with the hosted or Enterprise offering, so the 'full platform' is not shown to be open source. The documented local processing of evaluation data is tied to Unleash Enterprise Edge. missing for 10: evidence that the complete feature set (RBAC, change requests, SSO) ships in the open-source distribution, explicit documentation that evaluation and telemetry data stay on-prem for the OSS server, hands-on self-hosting corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can self-host the full flag platform from an open-source distribution, keeping evaluation data on my infrastructure

citations.quote: This guide helps you set up Unleash Open Source or Unleash Enterprise in your own environment using Docker.
To start the Unleash server, clone the Unleash repository and start the server with Docker Compose
user data (PII) used for targeting rules (like user IDs, emails, or IPs) is processed within the Edge node and never sent to the Unleash Cloud or your upstream instance
This gives you access to a hosted instance with unlimited projects and environments and features such as role-based access control, change requests, single sign-on, and SCIM
